raw.details:
HackCult ’26 | National-Level Hackathon

Presented by Blithchron ’27, IIT Gandhinagar, in strategic partnership with NxtWave

1. About the Hackathon

HackCult ’26 is a national-level hybrid hackathon that challenges student innovators to develop practical, technology-driven solutions to real-world problems. Explore sustainability or digital heritage, collaborate with fellow innovators, and turn your ideas into working solutions.

  • Organiser: Blithchron ’27, IIT Gandhinagar

  • Strategic Partner: NxtWave

  • Mode: Hybrid

  • Phase 1: Online

  • Grand Finale: IIT Gandhinagar, Palaj, Gujarat

  • Total Prize Pool: ₹30,000 in Amazon Gift Cards

  • Registration Fee: Free

    Track 1: Green Energy & Sustainability

    Mission LiFE engagement tools, citizen energy tracking, and gamified carbon footprint platforms.

    Track 2: Culture & Digital Heritage

    Interactive 3D architectural twins, vision transformer OCR for historical manuscripts, and dynamic mapping for on-the-ground travel exploration.

2. Eligibility & Team Formation

  • Open to currently enrolled university and college students.

  • Working professionals are not eligible.

  • Individual participation or teams of up to 4 members are permitted.

  • Cross-college and cross-year teams are allowed.

  • Team composition will be frozen once registrations close.

3. Benefits for All Participants

  • $500 in Adaption Platform credits per participant for dataset generation, augmentation, and custom model training, including multilingual data across 242 languages.

  • Exclusive technical workshop on data optimisation and custom model training hosted by Adaption.

  • Certificates of Participation for valid Phase 1 submissions.

  • Certificates of Excellence for Phase 2 finalists.

  • Mentorship checkpoints with experts during the online sprint.

4. Event Timeline

  • 22 October 2026, 11:59 PM: Registration deadline

  • 23 October, 5:00 PM: Virtual inauguration and kick-off

  • 23 October, 6:30 PM: 48-hour coding sprint begins

  • 24–25 October: Mentorship checkpoints

  • 25 October, 6:30 PM: Phase 1 submission deadline

  • 2 November: Finalists announced

  • 14 November, 10:45 AM–1:15 PM: Technical booth demonstrations at IIT Gandhinagar

  • 14 November, 3:00–5:00 PM: Grand Finale stage pitches and jury Q&A

5. Submission Requirements

Phase 1: Online Screening

Deadline: 25 October 2026, 6:30 PM

Teams must submit:

  1. Public GitHub Repository: Complete codebase with commits from the hackathon window, a comprehensive README, architecture diagrams, and setup instructions.

  2. Video Walkthrough: An unlisted YouTube video demonstrating the working features of the solution.

  3. Pitch Deck: Problem overview, system architecture, database schema, and scalability potential.

The goal is to demonstrate a functional baseline solution with sound technical logic.

Phase 2: Offline Grand Finale

Date: 14 November 2026 | Venue: IIT Gandhinagar

Round 1 - Technical Booth Demonstration (10:45 AM–1:15 PM)

  • Demonstrate a live application on deployed servers or mobile devices.

  • Showcase functionality using dynamic inputs rather than hardcoded dummy data.

  • Defend backend scalability, API performance, database design, and security.

Round 2 - Grand Finale Stage Pitch (3:00–5:00 PM)

  • 5-minute presentation followed by 3 minutes of jury Q&A.

  • Demonstrate product impact, scalability, and readiness for real-world deployment.

6. Judging Criteria

Phase 1 - Online Screening

  • Technical Execution & Code Quality: 40%

  • System Architecture & Scalability: 30%

  • UI/UX: 20%

  • Innovation & Problem Fit: 10%

Phase 2 - Technical Booth Demonstration

  • Live System Resilience: 35%

  • Code Integrity & Originality: 25%

  • Architectural Depth: 25%

  • Domain Alignment: 15%

Phase 2 - Stage Pitch

  • Product Impact & Scalability: 40%

  • Clarity of Pitch: 30%

  • Jury Defence & Q&A: 30%

Judging Panel: NxtWave experts, including senior developers, product managers, and mentors.

7. Rules & Guidelines

  • Participation is completely free.

  • All core logic must be developed during the 48-hour coding sprint.

  • AI development tools, including ChatGPT and Copilot, are permitted; teams must be able to explain and defend their code.

  • Team membership is frozen after registration closes.

  • Track selection is not locked at registration. Teams must finalise their track choice during Phase 1 submission.

  • Travel, food, and accommodation for the offline finale must be arranged and funded by participants.

8. Contact & Support

For queries or assistance, contact:

Email: blithchron@iitgn.ac.in
